items.title: Anonymous POST /api/catalog/items returns 401 and creates no item
items.reason: The bug's first reproduction step: anyone on the network could create products (`201`). This is the core security regression guard for `CreateItem`. It runs on the test stack because the AC names `e2e/teststack/catalog-admin.spec.ts` and the protection depends on the deployed JWT configuration; the functional fixture authenticates every request, so it cannot observe anonymous behavior.

items.title: Anonymous v2 PUT /api/catalog/items/1 returns 401 and leaves item 1 unchanged
items.reason: The bug's second step: anyone could change products and prices (`201`). Guards `UpdateItem-V2`. Checking that the stored price is unchanged proves the request was rejected before any write, not after. Test stack layer for the same reason as TC-BUG-4-01.

items.title: Anonymous v1 PUT /api/catalog/items returns 401 and leaves item 1 unchanged
covers: Technical Notes: UpdateItemV1 mapped with no RequireAuthorization()
items.reason: The Technical Notes list `UpdateItemV1` (`PUT /api/catalog/items`, id in the body) as a separate unprotected mapping. It is a distinct route from the v2 PUT, so protecting one does not protect the other; it needs its own case.

items.title: Anonymous DELETE /api/catalog/items/1 returns 401 and item 1 still exists
items.reason: The bug's DELETE step returned `204`: anyone could remove products. Guards `DeleteItem`; the follow-up read proves nothing was deleted. Test stack layer for the same reason as TC-BUG-4-01.

items.title: POST with a malformed bearer token returns 401 and creates no item
covers: Expected: 401 Unauthorized for callers that are not authenticated
items.reason: Requiring authentication must mean a valid token, not merely the presence of an `Authorization` header. A misconfigured JWT handler (for example a missing `Identity:Url` on the test stack) could accept or crash on a bad token. Runs on the test stack so the real JwtBearer configuration of catalog-api is exercised.

items.title: Anonymous price change publishes no ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEvent
covers: Actual: a price change also publishes ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEvent
items.reason: The story calls out that an anonymous price change also publishes `ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEvent`, which propagates the forged price to baskets. The event is recorded in the catalog database's `IntegrationEventLog` table (`UseIntegrationEventLogs()` in `CatalogContext`), which the functional layer can query directly against its real Postgres. This needs a `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` client built without `AutoAuthorizeStartupFilter` (the default `CatalogApiFixture` authenticates every request) and sends no `Authorization` header.

items.title: Authenticated POST creates an item (201 with Location)
covers: Expected: authorized callers can change the catalog (create)
Decisions: catalog scope unused; a token from the issuer for another scope is accepted
Acceptance Criteria 2: the rest of the file still passes
items.reason: The fix must lock out anonymous callers without locking out legitimate ones: if JWT validation is misconfigured (wrong `Identity__Url` / issuer on the test stack), every write would return `401` and the catalog could no longer be managed. Only the test stack issues real Identity.API tokens to a deployed catalog-api. The story's Decisions state that no client may request the `catalog` scope yet and that writes accept any token from the issuer (`ValidateAudience=false`), so this case deliberately uses an `orders`-scoped token: a `401` here would mean catalog-api started checking the scope or audience, which would lock out every client.

items.title: Authenticated v2 PUT changes the price of item 99 (201)
covers: Expected: authorized callers can change the catalog (update)
items.reason: Confirms an authenticated caller can still update an item and its price through the protected `UpdateItem-V2` route on the deployed stack. Uses item 99 so the anonymous cases' assertions on item 1 are not affected.

items.title: Authenticated DELETE removes item 101 (204, then 404)
covers: Expected: authorized callers can change the catalog (delete)
items.reason: Confirms the protected `DeleteItem` route still works for an authenticated caller on the deployed stack. Item 101 is used so no other case depends on it.

covers: Technical Notes: Identity.API has no catalog API scope

It is a pure configuration fact, so the in-process unit layer (`tests/Application.UnitTests/IdentityConfigurationTests.cs`) is the cheapest check.

items.reason: Expected says anonymous callers get `401`, without exception. If the check ran after the item lookup, anonymous callers could probe which ids exist (`404` vs `401`). Separate from TC-BUG-4-04 because it checks ordering of authorization before the not-found branch.
